references.text: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the same expression used in Judges 2:12
The warning against following other gods from the peoples around them, and that this would provoke the Lord's anger
The warning against turning away from the Lord to serve and worship other gods, which would provoke the Lord's anger
Describes how the people abandoned their covenant with the Lord and served other gods they did not know
The prophecy that the people would leave the Lord and follow foreign gods, and that God's anger would be kindled against them
Joshua's warning to the people about the consequences of leaving the Lord and serving foreign gods
Solomon left the Lord and worshiped other gods, the same sin described in Judges 2:12
The Israelites left the Lord their God who had brought them out of Egypt and served other gods
God accuses the people of having abandoned him and worshiped other gods
The people have left the Lord, the source of living water, to hew out broken cisterns
The women wept over Tammus, an example of idolatry that provoked the Lord's anger
